subject: Post-demo SLO confirmation & MAP commitments
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@fintechco.com>, Ben Harris <ben.harris@fintechco.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo SLO confirmation & MAP commitments

Hi Samantha / Ben —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and appreciate the transparency on your tail latency constraints and streaming checklist. Quick recap from our side and a short mutual action plan so we keep momentum.

1) SLO targets you confirmed on the call (please flag if I captured anything incorrectly):
   - 95th percentile single-token latency ≤ 45ms (tokenization + model inference) for short responses (mean tokens ~40)
   - End-to-end response latency (client -> app -> model -> first-streamed token) ≤ 120ms for streaming flows
   - Sustained throughput target: 600 reqs/min (peak bursts to 1,200 reqs/min for 3–5 min windows)
   - Concurrent active sessions target: 150 active websocket streams (typical model state cached)

2) Constraints and must-haves you emphasized:
   - No external PII leaves your VPC (we'll use Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering)
   - Audit logs and token-level cost breakdown for the pilot window

3) Next steps (Mutual Action Plan - short):
   - By 04/19: Redwood to share an SLO checklist and simulated load test plan (attached: demo-slo-checklist.pdf) — owner: Hannah
   - By 04/21: FinTechCo to confirm streaming protocol (websocket vs server-sent events) and identify a test client — owner: Ben
   - Week of 04/26: Redwood to run a targeted load test using your sample payloads and return a load summary + recommended config (autoscaling, batching, quantization) — owner: Dylan

4) Decision criteria you called out:
   - Meet streaming latency target under 80% of sustained load (i.e., 95p streaming token latency ≤ 100ms at 480 reqs/min)
   - Predictable cost per 1k tokens within 15% of our initial quote
   - No regressions on quality (we'll baseline with your 50-case eval set)

If the above looks right, we'll mark the MAP and move to the load run. I'll schedule a 30-min sync with your infra folks once we have the test client.

Attachments: demo-slo-checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
(408) 555-0134

Thanks Hannah — this looks good and aligns with our notes. Two clarifications from our side before you run load tests:

- For streaming: we prefer websocket but one requirement is that first-byte latency to client (including our edge) must be < 140ms; can you include an end-to-end breakdown in the report?
- For concurrency: the 150 active streams includes idle-but-open sockets; during peak business hours we expect ~100 of those to be actively sending/receiving tokens.

Also attaching a small sample traffic file we use for synthetic tests. Please use that for the load run.

One ask on compliance: we need to ensure audit logs include request IDs and model version. Happy to share an example schema.

Cheers,
Samantha
Director of Product, FinTechCo
Samantha Ortiz | samantha.ortiz@fintechco.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo SLO confirmation & MAP commitments

Quick update from infra after an initial dry run against the sample payload:

- Short summary of results (attached full CSV: load-test-summary-20270419.csv):
  * Sustained 600 reqs/min: PASS for 95p token latency (measured ~42ms avg 95p) on a 4xA100 Dedicated node config with our default batching and prefix cache
  * Burst to 1,200 reqs/min for 3 minutes: PASS but required autoscaling to +1 node after ~90s; 95p increased to ~85ms during the autoscale window
  * Streaming first-byte (end-to-end, simulated edge hop): 95p ~118ms when client is in same region; cross-region simulated edge added ~35ms median (95p ~155ms) — this is expected; recommend colocating edge or using region with lower network RTT.
  * Concurrency: simulated 150 open sockets (100 active): memory + KV-cache pressure observed when >160 active (recommend soft cap at 180 total sockets per node for current config)

- Audit logs: we can include request_id and model_version in the retained logs and will include a sample schema in the run report.

Recommended next steps for the MAP:
 - Confirm preferred region for pilot (us-west-2 preferred to hit 120ms target reliably) — owner: FinTechCo
 - Plan a single coordinated pilot window (2 hours) where we run sustained 600 r/m and 2x burst windows and capture traces — owner: Redwood (Dylan)
 - If cross-region clients are essential, discuss edge-colocation options and cost impact with Redwood infra (estimate to follow) — owner: both

I'll attach the CSV and a brief config diff for the node sizing. If this looks good I'll propose two 2-hour slots next week for the pilot.

-Dylan
